claim: Machine-checked proof (a kernel such as Lean or Isabelle) gives an exact verifier; every recent prover result is reportable only because of it.
agent_test: On exact tasks (formal math, code with tests) compare verify-then-accept vs self-judged accept at equal tokens; count false accepts.

claim: More samples and search raise the solve rate steadily: DeepSeek-Prover-V2-671B 82.4% (pass@32) to 88.9% (pass@8192) on miniF2F-test; GPT-f gained 9.2 points from more search; Baldur 40.7% at 64 samples.
agent_test: Plot accuracy vs token budget (N=1,4,16,64) with an exact checker; look for the knee.

claim: Returns from sampling diminish and cost a lot: the last 6.5 points of DeepSeek-V2 cost 256x more samples; reasoning mode used about 9x more tokens (6751.9 vs 761.8 per proof).
agent_test: Set a stop rule when marginal gain per token falls below a threshold; test vs fixed N.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Pairing a generator with a symbolic tool beats either alone: Thor 57.0% vs LM 39.0% vs Sledgehammer 25.7% on PISA, 8.2% solved by neither alone; Magnushammer 59.5% vs 38.3%.
agent_test: Give the agent an exact solver (SAT, CAS, calculator) and compare to pure-text reasoning at equal tokens.

claim: Retrieval of relevant facts helps, mostly in-distribution: LeanDojo ReProver 51.2% random split vs 47.6% without retrieval, but novel_premises 26.3% vs 23.2%; GPT-4 zero-shot 29.0% and 7.4%. Gap check: in-project step-wise retrieval (Rango) keeps unseen-project accuracy at 32.0% vs 36.8% file-wise; LeanAgent continual updating proved 155 sorry theorems; neural clause guidance in Vampire falls below default off-distribution.
agent_test: Hold out new lemmas: test library retrieval on items whose needed lemma was not seen in earlier tasks.

claim: Verifier-feedback repair gives a small gain: Baldur repair +1.5% at equal compute; Goedel self-correction about +2 points (88.1 to 90.4%).
agent_test: Compare one revise round with error text vs one extra independent sample at equal tokens.

claim: Decomposing into an informal sketch plus formal subgoals helps: DSP raised miniF2F-test from 20.9% (Sledgehammer+heuristics) to 39.3% (human sketch), 37.7% (Minerva 62B); dropping the automated prover costs 9.8 points; Hilbert recursion reached 99.2% with Gemini 2.5 Pro vs 49.1% for that model alone.
agent_test: Ablate a sketch-then-fill step vs a direct attempt on multi-step exact tasks at equal tokens.

claim: The planner/reasoner quality matters a lot: Hilbert with gpt-oss-120b solved 88/660 PutnamBench vs 462/660 with Gemini 2.5 Pro (same prover). Gap check: Hilbert depth ablation 75% (prover only) to 98.4% at depth 2; retrieval ablation 99.2% vs 97.9% with 2.3M vs 4.0M reasoner tokens (a clean ablation, so the 43% fewer tokens is a retrieval effect). Matched-token decomposition ablation still missing.
agent_test: Swap the planner model inside the scaffold; measure sensitivity.

claim: Benchmarks saturated fast: miniF2F-test 29.9% (Thor 2022) to 99.6% (Seed-Prover 2025); PutnamBench 1/640 (GPT-4, 2024) to 331/657 (Seed) and 462/660 (Hilbert, 2025). Numbers from different eras should not be compared.
agent_test: Use fresh held-out items for any claim about scaffold gains.

claim: Neurosymbolic translation to a solver helps on shallow natural-language logic but is not uniformly better: Logic-LM +18.4 over CoT (GPT-3.5); LINC ProofWriter 98.3% (GPT-4); but LINC vs CoT on FOLIO GPT-4 72.5 vs 75.3 (McNemar p=0.58); FOL syntax errors 38%/24%/13%. Gap check (SATLM): big gains on constraint tasks (GSM-SYS 69.4 vs 43.4 program-aided) but none on plain GSM (71.8 vs 72.7).
agent_test: Translate-to-solver arm vs CoT arm on FOLIO-like items with a GPT-4-class model; log translation failures.

claim: The translation step is the weak link: executable rate on AR-LSAT GPT-4 is 32.6% (39.8% after refinement); FOLIO 79.9%; easy AMC items were hard to formalise in Seed-Prover.
agent_test: Count unformalisable items; route them to the informal path and measure cost.

claim: Formal proving beats informal reasoning only in part: on AIME 24-25 (15 problems) DeepSeek-Prover-V2 formal solved 6 vs 8 for DeepSeek-V3 informal majority vote; o1 and Gemini thinking solved 0 of 50 IMO geometry problems that AlphaGeometry 2 solved 42 of.
agent_test: On a mixed set, compare formal route vs majority vote at equal tokens; the AIME sample (15) is tiny.

claim: Small open provers can beat huge ones with better data: Goedel-Prover-V2-8B 84.6% pass@32 above DeepSeek-Prover-V2-671B 82.4%.
agent_test: Not a scaffold claim; data and training dominate at small sizes.

claim: Step-wise tree search vs whole-proof generation is unsettled: Baldur whole-proof 47.9% vs search 39.0% (Isabelle); DeepSeek-V1.5 whole-proof 60.2% vs 63.5% with MCTS; at 3200 samples V1.5-RL 54.9% matched a tree-search system at 54.5%. Gap check: ProofAug reports RMaxTS only <0.2% above naive retry at 3200 samples (sample-matched, Isabelle, 7B); token-matched evidence still missing.
agent_test: Equal-token compare: N independent attempts vs a small tree with checker pruning.

claim: Classic resolution/saturation provers solved real open problems such as the Robbins conjecture (EQP, 8 days, 1996), but no number-bearing CASC evidence was captured.
agent_test: Gap: no CASC numbers.

claim: Autoformalisation is feasible but lossy: Wu et al. 25.3% of problems translated perfectly; proof rate 29.6% to 35.2% with autoformalised data. Gap check: on miniF2F the full pipeline reached about 36% vs 97% and 69-71% for the parts; an LLM judge said 97% faithful where humans said 66%; correcting the benchmark lifted effective accuracy 40% to 70%.
agent_test: Measure translation fidelity with a round-trip check.

claim: Suggest-then-verify tooling reduces human effort: Lean Copilot automated 74.2% of steps vs 40.1% for Aesop, 2.08 vs 3.86 manual steps.
agent_test: Low priority; shows tool suggestion plus verify beats rule-based automation.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Training-free agent scaffolds on frontier general models now reach or beat trained provers on hard formal benchmarks, at tens of dollars per problem: Aleph GPT-5.2 agentic 637/672 at $54 (pass@2), 668/672 at $68 (pass@3) vs DeepSeek-Prover-V2-671B 47/672 and Seed-Prover 1.5 581/672 (about $168). Theo (Claude Opus 4.7) solved 32/32 random PutnamBench items. No token-matched comparison exists.
agent_test: Run a fixed-token scaffold (sample, kernel check, error-fed repair, decompose) with a frontier model on 30 Lean items; compare with a single long reasoning pass at equal tokens.

claim: Cost per verified proof is high and depends on accounting: about $5 (subscription) to $29 (API list) for Theo, $39 Hilbert, $54-68 Aleph, $168 Seed-Prover 1.5, $18 DeepSeek-V2-671B at pass@1024 (authors' estimates).
agent_test: Log tokens and dollars per accepted proof; set a per-item ceiling and stop.

claim: A stop/restart rule learned from failed Lean attempts saves about 28.9% cost at parity accuracy (oracle 62.0%); decomposition plus lemma attempts more than doubled solves for an 8B prover (23 to 48 of 85).
agent_test: Compare fixed N attempts with a rule that restarts decomposition after repeated same-error failures, at equal total tokens.

claim: LLM-judged back-translation overstates autoformalisation fidelity: 97% by LLM judge vs 66% by human Lean experts; model round-trip checks are not a safe fidelity test.
agent_test: Seed 20 known-wrong formalisations; count how many a self round-trip check accepts.

claim: Learned guidance and retrieval transfer poorly across distributions: Vampire neural clause selection is below the default off-distribution; a joint model recovers 95-101% of dedicated models.
agent_test: Test any retrieval or hint helper on a held-out task family before relying on it.
